verdict: The lesson is at the 8 rung: 16/16 tests pass under the documented npm test, every headline number I recomputed from data.js matches the copy and TEST_REPORT exactly (1.8-point gap = 1.8%/45% of axis height; convenience n=500 at 56.4% late-library vs 25.2% population; r 0.81 to 0.26/0.10/0.31 within seasons), and all seven deliverables are present and truthful. The blocker is deploy parity: the live GitHub Pages preview serves an older revision than the archive (start copy 'fails all three on purpose' vs 'at least two of the three'; A2 hint 'about 25%' vs '25.2%'), failing Definition of Done #5. Re-push and hard-verify those two strings, and I would assign the lesson to a Year 11 class tomorrow.

keep: Seeded generators as the single source of truth — mulberry32 + Box-Muller with documented seeds (data.js:9-25, 46-59, 85-99; seeds 20260914 and 3141), with every displayed number recomputed by pure model.js functions; I re-ran it and 1.8%/45%, 56.4% vs 25.2% and r 0.81 to 0.26/0.10/0.31 all match the copy and TEST_REPORT exactly.

The honest answer keys and nuance copy — FRAMING_CHANGED/FRAMING_SAME (model.js:40-41), SAMPLING_ANSWER = 'bias' (model.js:74), CORRELATION_ANSWER = 'third' (model.js:95), with feedback that says a non-zero axis is not automatically deceptive (app.js:214), a bigger biased sample measures the wrong group more precisely (app.js:290), and association alone shows neither cause (app.js:352).

The framing metric that cannot lie — 'gap as drawn (share of the axis height)' (model.js:30-32) plus axis limits that provably cannot clamp a data point (AXIS_MIN_MAX/AXIS_MAX_MIN, model.js:39, asserted in tests/model.test.mjs:21-24).

Honest handling of free text — reviewConclusion checks presence, evidence words and over-claiming and states it does not judge reasoning (model.js:106-119, index.html:278), and the A3 justification is required before the keyed answer is accepted (app.js:347-350).

State handling that survives real use — localStorage load with corrupt-JSON fallback (app.js:21-29), two-click confirm reset with no reload (app.js:107-119), ?screen= URL routing (app.js:83), and notebook entries keyed by id so re-checking never duplicates them (app.js:70-72).
gap_to_10: Seeing Theory (Brown) at the top of the ladder: its manipulations are the concept — you drag the sample size and the sampling distribution builds under your hand — and Ciechanowski's layered figures reveal structure progressively. Here the charts are conventional (line chart, dot plot, scatter) and feedback arrives as text boxes: the axis change is shown before/after rather than as a continuous transformation, and the sampling bias is read off a table rather than seen in the selection mechanism. A 10 would make the manipulation itself carry the insight — the gap visibly stretching while the numbers stay pinned, and the library-door pool visibly over-picking late-library students as you draw.
